scenes.narration: This is AnyOrder. A uniform-price batch-auction exchange in Fe whose fills are independent of transaction order, so a sandwich has no ordering to exploit.

scenes.visual: `/` the sandwich-contrast section scrolled into view; the page's own "Recorded on a local Anvil chain" label stays in frame
scenes.gate: the recorded label and the recorded pool profit figure (as the page formats `web/public/recorded/sandwich.json`) are in the final frame
scenes.narration: On a constant-product pool, the order of transactions sets your price. A searcher buys just before your trade and sells just after it, and keeps what your trade moved.

scenes.narration: Here is the evidence, on the real compiler. fe test, filter sandwich: six tests pass. The test source asserts that a pool sandwich nets the attacker 0.00809 ETH; the exact figure is on screen. The same orders in one batch clear at 0.011 either way. The victim's fifteen tokens cost exactly 0.165 ETH either way, and the attacker ends at minus one wei and zero tokens. Then the permutation filter: 256 shuffles of the pure rule and 256 shuffled interleavings at contract level. Same price, same fills, every time.

scenes.narration: This panel is where the guarantee stops. It holds under condition C: equal legs, priced outside every other order. A one-sided buy still moves the price, from 0.011 to 0.012 ETH. That is market power, not ordering.

scenes.narration: Now the lifecycle. A built-in trader, an Anvil dev account, places an order into the open batch. The dev-chain control advances time to close the batch. Anyone can clear it, and the contract picks one price. Then the trader claims the fill. Placing and clearing declare no Call, so they cannot move funds.

scenes.visual: `/` the Fe highlight section: the `select_price` signature and the `uses` table
scenes.gate: the section's text includes `select_price` and a `uses` row with `place` showing no `Call`; both fully in frame, legible at 1080p
scenes.narration: Fe makes that claim checkable from the signature. select_price, the clearing function, declares no effects at all: it cannot read the clock, a caller or storage, or move funds. The handlers that place orders and clear batches declare no Call, and the compiler enforces it. Only deposit token and withdraw hold Call.
